A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TextOCVP work. All 21 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Methods, experiments, equations, and illustrations can be matched despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original CATER and CLIPort prediction results, architectural ablations, robustness evaluations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports video-quality measurements, inference timings, and artifact-cropping results.

M1.justification: The documented reconstruction objectives in Eqs. (4)–(5) change from unspecified, unsquared norms to squared L2 errors. This is a limited objective-specification revision; the architecture and prediction procedure are retained. The PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed or the formulas were corrected.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CATER-hard, CLIPort Put-Block-In-Bowl, and the unseen-color and increased-object-count scenarios. However, v2 Section 4.1 describes CATER scenes as containing 2–8 objects, versus 3–8 in v1 and v2 Appendix D.1. An actual coverage change versus a textual error cannot be resolved.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparator sets are retained: OCVP-Seq, Non-OC TF/Non-OC, MAGE, MAGE_DINO, and SEER. V2 Table 5 quantifies the original-versus-DINO MAGE comparison already discussed in v1 Appendix C.1. Renaming Non-OC TF and counting the MAGE variants separately do not introduce new methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds JEDi throughout the principal benchmark and ablation evaluations, replacing PSNR in the ablation tables. The text-encoder ablation changes from 9-frame to 19-frame prediction. New protocols evaluate cropped images and inference latency for one and nine predicted frames, substantially extending what the evaluation measures.

E4.justification: V2 adds an artifact-cropping control (Table 9), includes fine-tuned T5 on CATER (Table 2b), quantifies the MAGE adaptation (Table 5), and adds an eight-object qualitative example (Figure 9b). These extend existing analyses; color/object-count robustness and attention visualizations were already present in v1.

E5.justification: V2 Table 7 introduces average inference times accompanied by ± values. V1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. The repetition count and meaning of ± are unspecified, so this does not establish additional training runs or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: TextOCVP's CATER nine-frame SSIM/LPIPS changes from 0.924/0.035 to 0.922/0.036. Ablation values also change, including eight-slot CLIPort SSIM from 0.890 to 0.946. Substantial new entries include JEDi and extended PSNR comparisons, text-encoder results under the revised horizon, MAGE-variant scores, timings, and cropped-image scores. Existing CLIPort benchmark SSIM/LPIPS values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Eqs. (4)–(5) mathematically revise the reconstruction-loss definitions to squared L2 terms and explicitly group image and feature losses. The remaining formal framework is retained, with no added or removed theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 promotes robustness to novel colors and object counts into the abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion. The central prediction and controllability claims remain. Renaming image-to-video generation as video prediction does not itself change the single-image, text-conditioned task.

C2.justification: V2 changes the frozen-T5 interpretation from best on both datasets to best on CLIPort and comparable on CATER. It adds efficiency and artifact explanations and links long-horizon instability partly to nine-frame training. Appendix F.2 also introduces an overbroad claim of consistently best LPIPS, contradicted by its 19-frame CLIPort results.

D1.justification: V2 discloses CLIPort learnable-parameter counts in Table 4 and clarifies final bilinear image resizing in Appendix B.1. V1's explicit statement that MAGE's speed parameter is omitted disappears. Most architectural details, training budgets, and code/video access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Jeong et al. (2025), expands diffusion-model discussion, and adds evaluation-metric references while removing selected background works such as DDLP and SPOT. It corrects the VQ-VAE attribution from ImageNet to Van Den Oord et al. Publication updates for existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change throughout, with extensive editing of the abstract, introduction, related work, and results discussion. Numerous numbered subsections become paragraph headings, qualitative discussion is reorganized, a metrics appendix is introduced, and limitations and future work receive separate subsections.

P2.justification: V2 reformats appendix text into two columns, merges the main benchmark tables, changes metric columns, and adds several supplementary tables. Figure 1 and qualitative annotations are revised. Existing evidence is also relocated: v1 Figure 11 becomes v2 Figure 7, and v1 Figure 5a becomes v2 Figure 10.

improvement.justification: JEDi evaluation, explicit baseline and parameter comparisons, timing measurements, and the artifact control make v2 more informative about prediction quality and practical tradeoffs. These benefits are tempered by reporting problems: Appendix F.2 claims consistent LPIPS superiority although Table 6 retains 19-frame CLIPort scores of 0.078 for TextOCVP versus 0.075 for MAGE_DINO. Undefined timing uncertainty and conflicting CATER descriptions also limit the improvement.
